content.text:
**No — nothing in forgemark sends "forgemark" in a User-Agent.** There isn't a single User-Agent reference in the repo's own code. What actually goes over the wire today:

- **Git smart-HTTP traffic** (clone/fetch/push, the bulk of the load) goes through go-git v6, whose HTTP transport stamps every request with `User-Agent: go-git/6.x` (`plumbing/transport/http/common.go:92` via `capability.DefaultAgent()`). So on the server side, forgemark runs look identical to any other go-git client.
- **Forgemark's own direct requests** set no User-Agent at all, so they get Go's stdlib default, `Go-http-client/1.1` (or `/2.0`):
  - the OAuth token POST in `internal/bench/creds.go:206`
  - the endpoint probe GET in `internal/bench/endpoint.go:73`

If you want requests identifiable as forgemark, there are two easy paths:

1. **Zero-code:** go-git's `DefaultAgent()` honors a `GO_GIT_USER_AGENT_EXTRA` env var, so exporting something like `forgemark/<version>` yields `User-Agent: go-git/6.x forgemark/<version>` on all git traffic (but not the two direct HTTP calls).
2. **One-point code fix:** everything — git ops and the direct calls — flows through the single shared client built in `newHTTPClient` (`internal/bench/runner.go:277`), because the agents pass it into go-git via `gitclient.WithHTTPClient(a.httpc)` (`internal/bench/agent.go:127`). Wrapping that client's transport in a RoundTripper that sets (or appends to) the User-Agent would tag every request forgemark makes, including overriding go-git's header since the RoundTripper runs last.

Happy to implement option 2 if you want it.

What changed:

- `internal/bench/runner.go:288` — `newHTTPClient` now wraps its `http.Transport` in a new `uaTransport` RoundTripper. Since every request (go-git clone/fetch/push via `WithHTTPClient`, plus the direct OAuth token and endpoint-probe calls) goes through this one client, the tag covers everything.

- A new `uaToken` in `internal/bench/runner.go` reads `vcs.revision` from Go's embedded build info (`debug.ReadBuildInfo`) and truncates it to 12 chars, so a normally built binary sends `forgemark/<sha12>` — git traffic becomes e.g. `go-git/6.x forgemark/4e0904ee94c7`. No version constant or ldflags needed; `go build` stamps it automatically.
- When there's no VCS info (under `go test`, or builds with `-buildvcs=off`), it falls back to the bare `forgemark`, and the test asserts against `uaToken` so it passes in both worlds.
- Verified end-to-end: I built the real binary into the scratchpad and confirmed it embeds `vcs.revision=4e0904ee...`; tests and `golangci-lint` are both clean.

One behavior worth knowing: a build from a dirty working tree still reports the last commit's SHA (Go sets a separate `vcs.modified` flag I'm not currently including). If you'd like dirty builds marked — e.g. `forgemark/4e0904ee94c7-dirty` — that's a three-line addition.
go debug package automagically reads it if binary is build from within a git managed folder?

Yes — but the "magic" happens at build time, not at read time. Since Go 1.18, `go build` (and `go install`) itself runs git while compiling a `main` package and stamps the result into the binary: it embeds `vcs=git`, `vcs.revision` (the full HEAD SHA), `vcs.time` (commit timestamp), and `vcs.modified` (whether the working tree was dirty). `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` doesn't touch git at runtime at all — it just parses that metadata back out of the running executable, so it works on any machine the binary is copied to, long after the checkout is gone.

The conditions for the stamp to be there:

- You're building a **main package**, and the **main module's** directory is inside a git checkout (hg, svn, bzr, and fossil are also supported) with the `git` tool available on the build machine.
- Nothing disabled it: `-buildvcs=false` (or `GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false`) turns it off, and `go build` will actually *fail* if it can't run git cleanly rather than silently guess — unless buildvcs is set to `auto` (the default), where a missing repo just means no stamp.
- It's a real build: **`go test` and `go run` binaries don't get VCS stamps** — that's exactly why `uaToken` needs the bare-`forgemark` fallback and why the test asserts against the variable rather than a literal SHA.

You can see what any binary carries with `go version -m <binary>` — that's what I ran after the change, which showed `build vcs.revision=4e0904ee...` in the compiled forgemark.

The practical caveats for forgemark: a binary built from a source tarball (no `.git`) or with buildvcs off reports nothing and falls back to plain `forgemark`; and a dirty-tree build still reports the last commit's SHA — the dirtiness is only visible in the separate `vcs.modified` setting, which the current code ignores (that's the `-dirty` suffix option I mentioned).

When `http.Client.Timeout` is nonzero and the Transport isn't one net/http recognizes (`*http.Transport`, http2), the client falls back to the legacy cancellation path: it allocates a cancel channel and spawns a bookkeeping goroutine **per request**. Since every measured upload-pack/receive-pack goes through this client, the UA tagging now adds avoidable scheduling/allocation overhead to the very numbers forgemark exists to measure. The reviewer suggests preserving the timeout via request contexts or avoiding the `Client.Timeout` + wrapper combination.

But it caught two design-level problems with the env-var approach that the trail reviewer and I both missed:

**The two that matter:**

C git ignores unknown tokens, but a strict receive-pack — like the Entire forge this tool exists to benchmark — could reject every push. This is inherent to go-git's env-var hook, not our bug per se, but we're the ones triggering it.

2. **The process-wide env var leaks into subprocesses** (`server/local.go:180`). `internal/server` imports `internal/bench`, so just starting `forgemark serve` seeds the var, and `runCLI` spawns `entire`/`gh` with the inherited environment — any go-git-based child gets tagged as forgemark, misattributing third-party traffic. Fix: scope the seeding to `cmd/forgemark`'s main and/or strip it from child envs.

- The test hardcodes go-git's private `"go-git/6.x "` prefix; any dependency bump breaks it. Should assert `HasSuffix(..., " "+uaToken)` (`runner_test.go:46`).

- The `len >= 12` guard drops short revisions (e.g. svn's decimal revs) *and* loses the `-dirty` marker with them; should truncate only when longer.
- Style: the init/var split relies on vars-before-init ordering and the doc comment sits on the wrong declaration.

**Refuted:** an untagged dumb-HTTP fallback path — forgemark's in-memory storage errors before that path can emit requests.
